itemVerdicts.evidence: queries.log:6 ran `sqlite3 -readonly ... "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM document_cache; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id) FROM document_cache;"` and report.md:6-7 reports it: "The local FRUS Explorer index: 552 volumes, 316,839 documents (`document_cache`)". I re-ran it: 316839|552, exact.

report.md:6 heads the memo with "**Corpus.** The local FRUS Explorer index: 552 volumes, 316,839 documents", naming the volume count and labelling the basis as local; report.md:341 adds "Everything above comes from the SQLite index and the bundled JSON." The conditionality is carried by "local" plus the count rather than spelled out as a caveat, which is the weakest form that still satisfies the item.

Every document citation is a pair, e.g. report.md:35 "`frus1881/d342` — Blaine to Lowell, 19 Nov 1881", report.md:64 "`frus1904/d542`", report.md:202 "`frus1903/d270`", report.md:213 "`frus1977-80v29/d162`". No title-only citations.

`rowid` appears nowhere in report.md (grep -i rowid: no match) and nowhere in queries.log as a selected or reported value; the only rowid in play is the FTS5 table's internal `content_rowid='rowid'`, which the memo never surfaces.

Every join is on the pair: queries.log:32 "JOIN document_sources s USING(volume_id,document_id)"; queries.log:50 "JOIN external_citations e USING(volume_id,document_id)" and "cross_references x ON x.source_volume_id=c.volume_id AND x.source_document_id=c.document_id"; queries.log:18 "LEFT JOIN document_dates dd ON dd.volume_id=f.volume_id AND dd.document_id=f.document_id".

Neither done nor disclaimed: grep of report.md for "front matter" and "editorial note" returns no match, and §6 "What I did not do" (report.md:339-353) lists five caveats, none about front matter. The headline set is unfiltered — running the memo's own query at report.md:163 I find 38 rows with `is_editorial_note=1` and 115 non-`dN` ids inside the 3,101 (`message-of-the-president` 27, `preface` 8, `message` 6, `terms` 4, `pm_dN` singletons). The one exclusion attempted anywhere, queries.log:43's `document_id NOT LIKE 'front%'`, is on an exploratory browse whose count is not reported, and would not have matched these ids in any case.

Neither `summary_text` nor `note_text` appears in queries.log or report.md; the memo reads `body_text`, `header` and `dateline` only (e.g. queries.log:21, queries.log:53). The FTS mirror it counts through does not carry either column.

Cross-references are used and unfiltered: queries.log:50 "--- cross refs out of cand:",con.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cand c JOIN cross_references x ON x.source_volume_id=c.volume_id AND x.source_document_id=c.document_id") — no `is_broken` predicate — and report.md:330 publishes the result: "the 3,101 documents carry 3,477 outbound cross-references and receive only 157 inbound." The column exists (`is_broken INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`) and the memo neither applied it nor said it had not; the true unbroken figure is 3,475.

report.md:349-350: "Counts here are FTS5 document counts with porter stemming, so `canal`/`canals` and `negotiate`/`negotiation` conflate. Phrase probes in quotation marks are exact." The probe design matches the statement — exactness-critical probes are quoted phrases throughout (queries.log:9, :24, :26, :46, :58).

`citation_era` is never touched in queries.log despite `document_sources` being joined twice (queries.log:32, :50); the periodisation instead uses the parsed document date, queries.log:18 "substr(COALESCE(dd.date_iso,''),1,3)||'0'", reported as such at report.md:303.

The two channels are counted separately and never added: report.md:117 "Of 3,101 topically-matching documents, 2,631 carry a parsed source note" versus report.md:131 "Footnote citations to material *outside* the printed record (`external_citations`): 686 on those documents". Separate queries too (queries.log:32 vs :50).

Operative queries are shown inline in the report (report.md:163, :176-179, :191-199) and the full statements are in the log in execution order. I traced and re-ran the load-bearing numbers: 6,957 (queries.log:7), 3,101 and 2,070 and 1,939 (queries.log:11), 161 `.812` rows (queries.log:36), 552/316,839 (queries.log:6) — all exact. One cosmetic discrepancy: report.md:289 displays the probe `"Remon" OR "Remón"` where queries.log:58 ran `'"Remon" OR "Remon"'`; unicode61 folds the accent so both return 71.

Shares carry both sides: report.md:117 "Of 3,101 topically-matching documents, 2,631 carry a parsed source note"; report.md:198 "in the core but NOT found by FTS 440 (43% of the core)" against report.md:192 "STRUCTURAL CORE 1,024 documents in 47 volumes"; report.md:240 "`persons` is populated for 285 of 552 volumes"; report.md:167-169 "a seeded random sample of 30 ... 28 are genuinely about the isthmus; 2 are lists of states ... ~93% precision".

report.md:241-243: "The canal's founding cast has **no** person records: Bunau-Varilla, Pauncefote, Herrán and Beaupré all return zero rows. The modern cast does: Torrijos Herrera, Omar (7 volumes), Linowitz, Sol M. (11), Tack, Juan Antonio (5)." The rows-possible check is the same statement, queries.log:39, which ORs all nine name patterns into one SELECT.

report.md:240 attributes a thin/zero result to index coverage rather than to history: "`persons` is populated for 285 of 552 volumes, and only 3,293 rows fall before `frus1930`"; report.md:347-348 flags an unverified axis: "I did not verify the completeness of `volume_structures` against the printed tables of contents"; report.md:326 separates source property from query artifact: "That is a real property of FRUS, not of my query".

queries.log:39 is a single SELECT ORing nine name patterns — torrijos/bunau/linowitz/bunker/pauncefote/herr_n/chamorro/tack/beaupr — so hits and misses come from one pass, and both are reported at report.md:241-243. Same shape at report.md:232-233 for the subject vocabulary: seven patterns searched in one pass (queries.log:31), "returns **exactly one entry**: `Suez Canal`" — the one hit proving the search could return rows while the topic returns none.

report.md:349-350 "Counts here are FTS5 document counts with porter stemming ... Phrase probes in quotation marks are exact" and report.md:340 "I did not read the TEI XML at `/Users/jbotts/Development/frus/volumes/`. Everything above comes from the SQLite index and the bundled JSON." Grain (document), matcher (FTS5 porter) and layer (index, not raw TEI) are all stated. Not stated: that the FTS mirror also indexes `header`, `dateline` and `source_note`, so a `canal` hit need not be in the body.

report.md:163 expands to seven spellings — "canal AND (isthmus OR isthmian OR Panama OR Nicaragua OR interoceanic OR \"inter-oceanic\")" — and report.md:142-157 publishes the split of the bare literal's hits: 6,957 for `canal`, 2,070 also matching Suez, 1,939 matching neither Suez nor any isthmian term (with the other canals named: Kiel, Kaiser Wilhelm, Grand Canal, Lynn Canal, Canal de Haro, Baltic, Massena), 3,101 on topic. Per-variant contributions were measured (queries.log:9 probes `isthmian`, `"interoceanic canal"`, `"ship canal"`, Tehuantepec, Chiriqui, Darien separately) but not published — the split reported is literal-versus-expansion, not variant-by-variant.

report.md:303 "Decade distribution of the 3,101 topical matches, by the index's parsed document date", and it names the residue: report.md:319 "(22 documents have no parsed date...)". The query is queries.log:18/:56, joining `document_dates.date_iso`, not volume years. Where volume years are used (the §1.4 spine, report.md:75-86) they are labelled as compilation headings, not as a date measurement.

The fold is never checked or disclaimed. report.md:249 names an Ed2 volume in passing — "50 in `frus1977-80v09Ed2` (Arab-Israeli Dispute)" — and treats it as just another volume; §6's caveats (report.md:339-353) do not mention second editions. It was not vacuous: running the memo's own query, frus1977-80v09Ed2 contributes 5 documents to the 3,101, so the headline set spans an Ed2 volume with no duplicate check.

report.md:117-129 establishes where the documents came from, from `document_sources` (queries.log:32): "Of 3,101 topically-matching documents, 2,631 carry a parsed source note. Repositories: Department of State 1763 / Carter Library 272 / National Archives 225 ...", plus the decimal-class axis at report.md:95-113 and the lot numbers at report.md:134.

report.md:131-133 establishes the footnote channel from `external_citations` (queries.log:50): "Footnote citations to material *outside* the printed record (`external_citations`): 686 on those documents, led by Carter Library / National Security Affairs (106), Carter Library / Presidential Materials (29), Johnson Library / National Security File (20)."

The two big counts are labelled and never summed, but the third is mis-signposted. report.md:131-134 runs the footnote sentence straight into "Lot files worth requesting: `78D300` (39 documents), `81F1` (27), `63D351` (11), `81D113` (11), `84D241` (10)" with no channel marker — yet those counts come from the source-note channel (queries.log:32, `s.lot_file_norm` joined from `document_sources`), not from `external_citations`. Sitting inside the external-citations paragraph, they read as where the editors' footnotes point when they are where the printed documents came from — the exact confusion the item forbids, and the item says *every* archival count must be labelled.

queries.log:33-35 open `/Applications/FRUS Explorer.app/Contents/Resources/decimal-class-labels.json` and walk its `schedules[0]` classes/countries/subjects tables to gloss real cited class numbers; the result is used at report.md:95-97 ("The 1910–49 schedule ... glosses subject suffix **`.812` as \"Canals\"**"). Weakest qualifying form, though: this is a gloss table, and none of the artifacts that resolve a citation to a NARA holding — central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json, series-facts-index.json, volume-sources-index.json, collection-authority.json — was opened at any point in the log.

report.md:134 names concrete lots to request: "Lot files worth requesting: `78D300` (39 documents), `81F1` (27), `63D351` (11), `81D113` (11), `84D241` (10)"; report.md:100-104 names concrete central-file classes (817.812 Nicaragua — Canals, 811f.812 Canal Zone — Canals, 883.812, 821.812).

Nothing is resolved. grep of report.md for NAID / "record group" / RG-number / "entry" / series returns no match at all; the archival identifiers stop at lot numbers and decimal classes quoted out of the source notes (report.md:100-104, :134) — precisely what the item excludes ("not merely quoted a lot number ... out of a source note"). No resolution artifact was consulted: central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json and series-facts-index.json are all present in the Resources directory the memo was reading from and none is opened anywhere in the 58-line log.

The share is published with both sides and against a control. report.md:142 "`canal` alone matches 6,957 documents", report.md:154 "`canal AND Suez` matches 2,070 — 30% of all *canal* documents", report.md:165 "→ **3,101 documents in 310 volumes**"; and the reverse direction against a structural control at report.md:192-198: "STRUCTURAL CORE 1,024 documents ... intersection with the topical FTS query 584 / in the core but NOT found by FTS 440 (43% of the core)", i.e. the literal-driven query accounts for 584 of 1,024 on-topic documents.

The change-claim at report.md:322-324 ("Two peaks, not one. The 1910s peak is tolls ... The 1970s peak is their surrender") sits on the full measured series at report.md:305-320, every decade 1860s-1980s counted, not just the endpoints; the comparative claim at report.md:325-328 is likewise two-sided ("**The 1900s decade ... is the third-smallest of the twentieth-century buckets (174)**" against the 1970s 684). The pre-FRUS claim at report.md:22-31 is backed by measurement of the earlier side too (57 Clayton-Bulwer, 98 for the 1846-instrument probe).

Two quotations have no retrieved row behind them. report.md:234-236 quotes the bundled subject index — "describes the tags as case-insensitive string matching, \"recall-oriented candidates rather than ground truth\"" — but queries.log:28, the only command that opens that file's top level, prints `list(d.keys())[:12]` and never a value; I confirmed the phrase is the value of the `provenance` key, which no logged command printed. report.md:332 likewise quotes an editorial idiom, "Continued from For. Rel. 1914, pp. …", with no volume_id/document_id and no query behind it. (The document quotations proper are clean — frus1881/d342 at report.md:35 is retrieved at queries.log:21, frus1901/d233 at queries.log:49, frus1904/d542 at queries.log:27.)

Reading counts are stated and kept distinct from the 3,101 matched: report.md:167 "I drew a seeded random sample of 30 (`random.seed(7)`) and read the snippets: 28 are genuinely about the isthmus; 2 are lists of states" (queries.log:51), and report.md:201 "A seeded sample (`random.seed(3)`) of 14" (queries.log:53), plus report.md:34 "Verified by reading, not inferred" over five named documents. Per-pass rather than a single aggregate figure, and honest that the 30 were snippets.

Each share carries its numerator and denominator where it is used: report.md:198 "in the core but NOT found by FTS 440 (43% of the core)" with "STRUCTURAL CORE 1,024 documents" four lines above in the same block; report.md:167-169 "sample of 30 ... 28 are genuinely about the isthmus ... ~93% precision"; report.md:154 "`canal AND Suez` matches 2,070 — 30% of all *canal* documents", the denominator being the 6,957 stated at the head of the same subsection (report.md:142) and named in the phrase itself. No bare share column anywhere.

The log claims a completeness it lacks. report.md:353 asserts "Every command is in `queries.log` beside this file, in order" and queries.log:1-3 promises the script bodies are "losslessly recoverable". But report.md:229 publishes "491 subjects over 877,817 document–subject pairs" and no logged command computes or prints it: queries.log:28 prints only `list(d.keys())[:12]`, queries.log:30 prints `len(v)` (=491, so that half is covered) and an 800-char dump, and queries.log:31 prints only the matching entries' `df`. I verified 877,817 is the sum of `df` over all 491 vocab entries — a figure nothing in the log sums. The provenance sentence quoted at report.md:235 is unprinted by any logged command for the same reason. So at least one published number and one published quotation came from outside the log while the log declares itself complete.

summary:
25 obeyed, 7 violated, 0 not_applicable — 25/32 = 78.1% compliance.

Violated: E1 (front matter / editorial notes neither excluded nor disclaimed — 38 editorial-note rows and 115 non-`dN` ids sit inside the headline 3,101), E3 (`cross_references` joined with no `is_broken` filter and no disclaimer; 3,477 published where 3,475 are unbroken), S5 (an Ed2 volume is named at report.md:249 and contributes 5 documents to the headline set, with no fold check), A3 (the lot-file counts at report.md:134 are drawn from the source-note channel but printed inside the external-citations paragraph with no channel label), A6 (nothing resolved — no NAID, record group, series or entry number appears anywhere, and none of central-files-index.json / lot-claimants-index.json / series-facts-index.json / volume-sources-index.json / collection-authority.json is opened in the 58-line log), P3 (two quotations with no retrieved row: the subject-index provenance sentence, whose value no logged command prints, and the "Continued from For. Rel. 1914" idiom), P6 (the log declares itself complete while at least one published number, 877,817, and one published quotation have no command behind them).

Notes bearing on the aggregate. The memo's arithmetic is sound where I could check it: 6,957 / 3,101 / 2,070 / 1,939 / 161 / 552 / 316,839 / persons-in-285-volumes / Suez Canal df 2,178 all reproduce exactly, and 584+440=1,024, 584+2,517=3,101 are internally consistent. Its strongest work is on the scoping items — P1 is obeyed in both directions (the literal `canal` costs 2,070 Suez documents and misses 440 of a 1,024-document structural core), and S1/R3 are satisfied by a single query carrying its own positive and negative control. Two obeyed verdicts are the weakest qualifying form and should not be read as strength: C2 discharges conditionality with the word "local" plus a count rather than a caveat, and A4 rests on `decimal-class-labels.json`, a gloss table, because no artifact that resolves a citation to a NARA holding was ever opened. Three of the seven failures (E1, E3, S5) are silent omissions on a full-corpus set, and the two P-item failures are the same underlying fact — material reaching the report from outside the log, both matching text documented elsewhere in the project verbatim.

POST-HOC, NOT SCORED — distinct NARA catalogue identifiers named as places to look beyond what FRUS printed: 0. The report contains no NAID, no record-group number, no series number and no entry number (grep for naid / "record group" / RG-number / "entry N" / series over report.md returns nothing on point). What it does name, none of which is a NARA catalogue identifier: five State Department lot numbers (78D300, 81F1, 63D351, 81D113, 84D241), nine central-file decimal classes (817.812, 811f.812, 883.812, 821.812, 711F.1914, 811F.504, 711.1928, 819.00, 819.77), and three archival collections by name (Carter Library / National Security Affairs, Carter Library / Presidential Materials, Johnson Library / National Security File). All are quoted out of source notes or footnote rows; none is carried through to a catalogue identifier a reader could request against.

itemVerdicts.evidence: report.md L10-14 runs and prints the coverage query: "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache; -- 552 | 316839 | 1012 | 8468"; queries.log L9 carries the same command verbatim. I re-ran it: 552|316839|1012|8468, exact.

report.md L16-20: "Your library holds **552 volumes / 316,839 documents** ... every count below is conditional on these 552 volumes. Where I say a thing is absent I mean absent from these 552." Volume count named, conditionality stated, and restated at L504-506.

Every citation is a pair, e.g. report.md L273-274 "frus1861/d300, frus1865p3/d34, frus1866p2/d241..." and L313-315 "`frus1881/d339`, `frus1881/d342`..."; the two quotations at L321 and L324 are cited as frus1881/d333 and frus1901/d233. No document is cited by title alone.

No rowid appears anywhere in report.md. The only rowid use is the FTS5 external-content link, e.g. queries.log L22 "JOIN document_cache d ON d.rowid = f.rowid" (frus_documents is declared content='document_cache', content_rowid='rowid'), and no rowid is ever carried out of a query or reported as identity: core_set.tsv, read_manifest.json and every cited id are (volume_id, document_id).

Every table-to-table join uses the pair: queries.log L101 "JOIN document_sources s ON s.volume_id=c.volume_id AND s.document_id=c.document_id"; L111-114 (document_dates + external_citations); L142-146 (cross_references on source_/target_ pairs); L163, L95 (document_dates). The document_id-alone trap (d1 exists in every volume) is never taken. Caveat noted at I2: the FTS-to-content join is on content_rowid, which is that table's defined mechanism.

report.md L22-23: "all DB counts **exclude** `is_front_matter=1` and `is_editorial_note=1` (denominator 307,359 documents)"; applied in every logged predicate (queries.log L32-33, L41, L67, L76) and in core.py, which I read. report.md L369-370: "2,971 unbroken outbound references from the core set (2 broken, excluded)"; queries.log L142-146 shows "WHERE x.is_broken=0" on every cross-reference query and separately counts the broken ones. I reproduced both: 2971 and 2.

This memo is the most heavily evidenced of its kind I have marked, and I checked it hard rather than taking it on trust. Everything I independently re-ran reproduced exactly: the coverage row (552|316839|1012|8468), the 306,619 working denominator, the positive/negative controls (98,499 documents in 551 volumes; 0), the eight-family share census line for line against share_out.txt, the 538-document/166-volume family, quarantine 847/213 and 226 in frus1961-63*, all fourteen rows of the §5 decade table including the per-1,000 rates, channels.sql's 69/62/62 archival counts, and the bundled-JSON facts (decimal-class-labels.json at schemaVersion 1 / 2026-08-11 / 9 classes / 198 countries with no name for country 42; `12` Public health, `124` Hygiene and sanitation, `1246` Hygiene of vessels and aircraft; no class-5 subject table; series-facts-index.json at schemaVersion 2, 695 series, 397 headings of which exactly one names health, and 2555709/302021/654171 all absent from byNaId; digitized-ranges-index.json 624 ranges with zero for 512/893/883/867/711; collection-usage coverage 264,464 / 74,914 / 190,407). Four quotations checked against document_cache are verbatim and all sit inside the ranges read2.sql–read4.sql fetched. The country-series roll counts (2,160 / 3,357 / 522 / 104 / 177) are exact. I found no false claim.

The single failure is P6, and it is a real one rather than a technicality. queries.log L1 declares "EVERY command that touched a surface, verbatim, in order", but L170 contains a literally elided `python3 -c` body, L108's pipe-to-python is unshown, and L147 admits "one inline block" that never appears — and those three are the commands behind two claims the memo makes (the `comp17` compilation node in §2 and the "chapter `<head>`s sit outside `<div type="document">`" reading in §7). The fallback P6 permits is also unmet for the JSON pass: five named scripts (gloss.py, archival.py, archival3.py, archival4.py, archival5.py) have no saved output, yet §8 publishes numbers from four of them. The memo is scrupulous elsewhere — it refuses to elide the 100-pair id list and says exactly which files hold it, it discloses two FTS5 queries that errored, and it quotes its scripts' SQL in full — which makes the residual elision look like an oversight rather than a habit, but the log does claim a completeness it lacks.

Two things worth flagging beyond the rubric. First, the memo caught the run's planted false friend and quantified it three ways (1 of 261 1960s `quarantine` documents carries disease vocabulary; 226 sit in frus1961-63* alone), then went further and found a second, unplanted one — the 1880s–90s pork controversy — by reading rather than by suspecting. Score: 23 obeyed, 8 violated, 1 not_applicable — compliance 23/31 = 74.2%. Violated: E1, R1, S4, S5, A2, A6, P5, P6.

This is a strong historical memo with a weak measurement discipline, and the two are separable. Its substance largely verifies: I reproduced the §2.1 term table exactly (sanitary 1331, quarantine 863, "sanitary convention" 84, "international sanitary" 65), the archival figures exactly (190,419 classed source rows, 163 documents with an 8xx.12* class and the whole per-country split, the 512.4 per-volume breakdown 6/3/4/3, the repository table 480/85/25/25), the semantic-map cluster 140 row (510 docs, eras 302/206/2), and every §7 corpus-integrity claim (694 TEI files, 552 indexed, 142 extras, median 2,483 bytes, none containing a sanitary/quarantine string). Six quotations checked against the DB are verbatim and inside the logged retrieval windows. The §3 compartment walk is real: my own volume_structures walk found 40 matching headings on a narrower key set, and the titles the memo lists appear verbatim.

What fails is verifiability and three checkable errors. (1) The log's own line-25 command, re-run verbatim, returns 1,421 documents where the memo reports 1,430 — and the same command returns `editorial 7`, a count the memo neither excludes nor mentions while it carefully drops 16 front-matter rows (E1, R1). (2) The headline Cuban-quarantine finding is mis-scoped: "279 quarantine hits in 1961–63 volumes ... 265 also mention Cuba" is the `frus196%` query of log L49, i.e. all 1960s volumes; the real frus1961-63 numbers are 231 and 230 (R1). (3) §6.1 tells the historian that "Browsing by subject cannot reach this topic" because "Not one subject name matches health, sanitary, disease...". That is false: document-subject-index.json carries Public Health (914 documents, 548 of them in pre-1950 volumes), Health care (641), Medical services (78), Tropical medicine and Biomedical research. The script that produced it is one of ~14 elided log entries, so the error was unreviewable by construction — which is the exact failure P6 exists to catch, aggravated by L6's claim that "everything below is checkable from queries.log" and by L42's logged command being broken shell that cannot have produced the text quoted from it.

The archival half is the thinnest: provenance is established from source notes (A1 solid, and reproduced exactly), but the footnote channel is queried once with a precedence-broken predicate and never reported, though it holds 118 references over 79 documents of this hit set (A2), and nothing is resolved to a catalogue record (A6). Ed2 duplicates are never checked, and the memo's own net matches both frus1969-76ve15p2 and its Ed2 twin (S5). Periodisation is by volume decade, disclosed but not on document dates (S4).

POST-HOC COUNT, not scored — DISTINCT NARA catalogue identifiers named as places to look beyond what FRUS printed: 0. The memo names no NAID, no record-group number (the strings "RG" and "Record Group" are absent), no series title, no entry number and no lot file.
